walkthroughs.body_html:
A circuit is a complete loop of wire with components, like a cell and a bulb.

If the loop is complete, charges flow and the bulb lights up.

If broken (a gap), no current flows.

The cell pushes charges around, and the bulb uses the energy carried.

Scientists use circuit symbols to draw circuits neatly:

Cell - one long, one short line.
Bulb - circle with a cross.
Resistor - rectangle.
Switch - line that can break.
Ammeter - circle with A.
Voltmeter - circle with V.

Current is the flow of electric charge. Like cars on a road. Unit: amps (A).

Voltage is the push that makes charges move. Like the slope of a hill. Unit: volts (V).

Higher voltage means more energy delivered per charge.

mcqs.q: If you double your distance from a point source of waves, what happens to the intensity?
options: It falls to one quarter — intensity follows an inverse-square law with distance from a point source.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
It halves — intensity is inversely proportional to distance.
It is unchanged because the wave doesn't lose energy.

mcqs.q: If a car doubles its speed, what happens to its kinetic energy?
options: No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
It quadruples (because KE = 1/2 mv^2 — kinetic energy is proportional to v^2).
Kinetic energy doubles because energy is proportional to speed.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.

mcqs.q: Is the cosmological redshift of distant galaxies a true Doppler shift?
options: No — it arises from the expansion of space stretching photon wavelengths during transit, not from the galaxy's motion through space.
No — it is caused by dust in space absorbing blue light.
Kinetic energy stays the same because mass hasn't changed.
Yes — it is the same Doppler shift as a moving siren on Earth.
